Section(s): References

Text and equations in reading order:
    The correct model equations used for all calculations presented in Seidel et al., (2018), are:
(C-11) r_{\mathrm{{C O}}}=(1-\phi)k_{1}\left(p_{\mathrm{{C O}}}p_{\mathrm{{H}_{2}}}^{2}-\frac{p_{\mathrm{{C H}_{3}\mathrm{{O H}}}}}{K_{\mathrm{{P}1}}}\right)\Theta^{\odot}\Theta^{\otimes^{4}}    [code: algebraic, computes r_{CO}, code proposes constitutive]
(C-12) r_{\mathrm{{C O}_{2}}}=\phi^{2}k_{2}\left(p_{\mathrm{{C O}_{2}}}p_{\mathrm{{H}_{2}}}^{2}-\frac{1}{K_{\mathrm{{P}2}}}\frac{p_{\mathrm{{C H}_{3}\mathrm{{O H}}}}p_{\mathrm{{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}}}{p_{\mathrm{{H}_{2}}}}\right)\Theta^{*^{2}}\Theta^{\otimes^{4}}    [code: algebraic, computes r_{CO_2}, code proposes constitutive]
(C-13) r_{\mathrm{R W G S}}=\phi(1-\phi)^{-1}k_{3}\left(p_{\mathrm{C O}_{2}}-\frac{1}{K_{\mathrm{P}3}}\frac{p_{\mathrm{C O}}p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}}{p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}\right)\Theta^{*}\Theta^{\odot}    [code: algebraic, computes r_{RWGS}, code proposes constitutive]
    Equation numbers refer to the corresponding equations in Seidel et al., (2018).
    The corresponding surface coverages are:
(C-14) \Theta^{\odot}=\left(1+\underbrace{K_{\mathrm{CO}}}_{\beta_{11}}p_{\mathrm{CO}}+\underbrace{K_{\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{OH}}^{\odot}}_{\beta_{12}}p_{\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{OH}}+\underbrace{K_{\mathrm{CO}_{2}}^{\odot}}_{\beta_{14}}p_{\mathrm{CO}_{2}}\right)^{-1}    [code: algebraic, computes \Theta^{\odot}, code proposes constitutive]

Symbols:
  r_{CO}: reaction rate of CO hydrogenation (computed)
  \phi: fraction of reduced surface centers [-] (computed)
  k_{1}: forward rate constant for CO hydrogenation (parameter)
  p_{CO}: partial pressure of CO (variable)
  p_{H_2}: partial pressure of hydrogen (variable)
  p_{CH_3OH}: partial pressure of methanol (variable)
  K_{P1}: equilibrium constant for the CO hydrogenation reaction (CO + 2 H2 ↔ CH3OH) expressed in terms of partial pressures (computed)
  \Theta^{\odot}: fraction of vacant catalytic sites (surface coverage) for the ⊙ site [-] (computed)
  \Theta^{\otimes}: fraction of surface sites of type \otimes (surface coverage) [-] (computed)
  r_{CO_2}: reaction rate of CO2 (computed)
  k_{2}: kinetic rate constant for reaction 2 (parameter)
  p_{CO_2}: partial pressure of CO2 in the gas phase (variable)
  K_{P2}: equilibrium constant for reaction P2 [-] (computed)
  p_{H_2O}: partial pressure of water vapor [bar] (variable)
  \Theta^{*}: fraction of reduced surface centers that are free (unoccupied) relative to total reduced surface centers [-] (computed)
  r_{RWGS}: reaction rate of reverse water-gas shift (RWGS) (computed)
  k_{3}: kinetic rate constant for the reverse water-gas shift reaction (parameter)
  K_{P3}: pressure equilibrium constant for the reverse water-gas shift reaction [-] (computed)
  K_{CO}: adsorption equilibrium constant for CO (parameter)
  K_{CH_3OH}^{\odot}: adsorption equilibrium constant for methanol on oxidized surface sites (parameter)
  K_{CO_2}^{\odot}: adsorption equilibrium constant for CO2 on a vacant site (parameter)

Model-wide assumptions (already recorded, do not repeat):
  - Catalyst deactivation neglected; only reactions (1)-(3) considered.
  - Langmuir‑Hinshelwood mechanism with adsorption, surface reaction, desorption.
  - Oxidized centers (⊙) are active for CO hydrogenation.
  - Reduced centers (∗) are active for CO₂ hydrogenation.
  - Total numbers of oxidized, reduced and hydrogen centers are constant.
  - Fast steps are at quasi‑equilibrium.
  - Quasi‑equilibrium assumption for fast adsorption/desorption steps.
  - Lumped kinetics for reactions (1)-(3).
  - Two alternatives for φ: quasistatic (Eq.22) or dynamic (Eq.28).

Laws: C-11, C-12, C-13, C-14

laws.description: Rate of CO hydrogenation expressed by a Langmuir–Hinshelwood kinetic expression that includes reactant and product partial pressures, surface coverages, and the fraction of oxidized sites.
laws.law_type_reason: It defines the CO hydrogenation rate using a Langmuir–Hinshelwood expression.

laws.description: Rate of CO2 hydrogenation expressed by a Langmuir–Hinshelwood kinetic expression that includes reactant and product partial pressures, surface coverages, and the fraction of reduced sites.
laws.law_type_reason: It defines the CO2 hydrogenation rate using a Langmuir–Hinshelwood expression.
laws.issue: The reverse term appears to be missing a factor of p_{CO_2} and has an extra division by p_{H_2}, inconsistent with the expected equilibrium expression for CO2 hydrogenation.
